profile.address: 1855, Gateway Boulevard, Concord, Contra Costa County, California, 94520
profile.reading:
This entry corresponds to 1855 Gateway Boulevard in downtown Concord, California, one of two twin ten-story office towers that make up the Concord Gateway complex, a roughly 600,000-square-foot Class A office development with an interior atrium lobby, on-site health club, and parking garage. The building is ordinary multi-tenant commercial office space, not a purpose-built data center, colocation facility, or hyperscale campus.

The listed operator, e360, is an IT consulting and managed-infrastructure services company (formerly Entisys Solutions, later Entisys360) that serves enterprise clients with cloud, security, virtualization, and managed-services support rather than operating data centers as a wholesale or colocation business. The company's own April 2016 rebrand announcement states that Entisys Solutions' corporate headquarters was, at that time, located in Concord, California, alongside additional offices in Sacramento, Irvine, and Pasadena, a footprint that matches this Gateway Boulevard address and explains why several business directories, including the company's Inc. 5000 profile, still list Concord as its headquarters city, with the company's roots tracing back to the 1990s and a 2008 merger with Agile360.

As of this writing, e360's current published contact page instead lists its headquarters in Irvine, California, with regional offices in Pasadena, Brentwood, and Sacramento (McClellan); Concord no longer appears among the company's currently listed locations. That gap between the older company material naming Concord as headquarters and the newer contact page naming Irvine suggests the company's headquarters designation, and possibly its lease at this address, changed at some point after 2016, though no public source identifies exactly when the Concord office was downsized, relocated, or dropped.

What can be said with confidence is that this is leased office space inside a large speculative office tower in downtown Concord, tied historically, and by several directory listings, to e360/Entisys, an IT services and managed-infrastructure reseller rather than a data center operator in the industry sense of owned white space, generators, and a dedicated cooling plant. No power capacity, server-room square footage, tenancy detail, or technical infrastructure for this address has been published by e360, by the building's commercial leasing brokers, or by any local permitting record identified in this research, consistent with its use as ordinary corporate office space rather than a mission-critical computing facility.

reading.body:
This record describes a facility in Concord, California attributed to e360, but e360's own website lists only offices in Irvine and Sacramento and identifies the company as an IT consulting and managed services provider, not a data center operator. No specifications for the Concord location appear in published sources, and the operator attribution does not match the company's stated service areas. This facility cannot be read as a data center campus until the operator and location are verified.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which 11 publish power consumption figures totaling 365 megawatts. This record ranks 12th by published megawatts in the state, below the group of 11 facilities with disclosed capacity. Without verified specifications, the facility's position in the state's infrastructure cannot be assessed.
